speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They have played a critical role in providing good quality healthcare for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When an outbreak occurs, hospitals must do two things.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First is to take steps to stop further transmission and care for the affected patients as best as they can.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The second is to review the processes at the individual and system levels and make improvements to reduce the risk of any recurrence.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Hepatitis C outbreak in the Singapore General Hospital (SGH) is a painful incident – painful to the patients, their families and our healthcare professionals.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The chief executive officer of SGH has apologised for the outbreak.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) and SGH are committed to caring for all affected patients by providing them with counselling, support and appropriate Hepatitis C treatment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The well-being of the affected patients and their family members remain our top priority.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: My Ministry will continue to work with SGH to ensure that they receive the necessary support and care.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Once again, let me apologise to the affected patients and their family members for this incident, and especially to those who have lost their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: To identify the cause of the outbreak and address the gaps, my Ministry has set up the Independent Review Committee (IRC) comprising experienced clinicians from different disciplines, with support from local resource persons and international experts, to determine the cause of the Hepatitis C outbreak and provide an objective and critical review of the response.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As a follow-up to the IRC report, both SGH and my Ministry have taken steps to address the gaps.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: MOH and SingHealth also instituted disciplinary procedures to hold our staff to account.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We set up independent human resource (HR) panels to examine the roles, responsibilities and actions of key MOH and SGH staff in relation to the incident and to recommend appropriate disciplinary actions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The SingHealth HR panel submitted its recommendations to the SingHealth Board.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Board decided that the junior and frontline healthcare staff would be required to undergo retraining and competency assessment to improve their infection prevention and control practices.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Board also decided to hold 12 SGH leaders, including senior management, responsible for their failure to enforce a strong infection control regime and incident escalation protocols within the hospital.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The MOH HR panel submitted its recommendations to the Public Service Commission (PSC).

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The disciplinary sanctions imposed on MOH and SGH staff included warnings, stern warnings and financial penalties.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When a warning is issued, it is lodged in the staff's service record.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: A stern warning is a more serious penalty.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Not only is it entered into the staff's service record, it has a negative bearing on his career, including future promotion and awards.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: A warning or stern warning may be given together with a financial fine.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But, Madam, the greatest penalty is not these disciplinary measures.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For everyone involved, including those who had provided direct care to the affected patients, we will carry with us the pain and regret of this incident for a long time to come.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is, therefore, important for MOH, our healthcare institutions and healthcare workers to learn from what went wrong and make sure the mistake is not repeated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Instead of naming individuals and developing a blame culture in our healthcare institutions, we need to encourage a learning culture to make our hospitals as safe as possible for the patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This culture of continual learning and improvement is important for enhancing patient safety and the quality of care.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Looking ahead, our focus is to improve our systems and processes to enhance infection control and strengthen detection and response to infectious diseases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Revealing the names of the officers and specific sanctions each individual received does not contribute to better care of our patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In deciding what to disclose, we have to bear in mind the longer-term impact on our healthcare system and healthcare workers and strike a careful balance.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Following the IRC's review, SGH has taken steps to improve infection control by enhancing its processes and strengthening cleaning and decontamination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: SGH also enhanced its education and retraining programmes for staff and implemented stricter monitoring of infection control practices.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: To verify that its systems are robust, SGH has engaged consultants from the Joint Commission International, a reputable accreditation and consultancy organisation, to conduct a thorough review Page: 14 and assessment of its clinical processes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are also sharing the lessons learnt from this outbreak with all hospitals and working with them to ensure that their infection control, risk management and escalation protocols are in place.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In December 2015, MOH set up a taskforce headed by Minister of State for Health, Mr Chee Hong Tat, to enhance the national healthcare system's ability to detect and respond to infectious disease outbreaks in hospitals and in the community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This includes setting up a National Outbreak Response Team comprising experts from across the healthcare fraternity.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This team will augment the efforts of healthcare institutions to deal with disease outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Other measures include simplifying processes for notification and reporting of infectious diseases by doctors and laboratories.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: MOH has also designated the Communicable Diseases Division to assume overall responsibility for overseeing surveillance of all infectious diseases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: While it is not possible to completely prevent outbreaks in hospitals, MOH and our healthcare institutions are determined to learn from the mistakes made so that we continue to improve our systems and processes to provide better and safer care to our patients.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
